set_aside.subject: R0-12 photo delivery failure classification
set_aside.text: “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: Which failures count as photo storage-unavailable: missing bytes, oversize content, an unlisted or unrecognizable media type, invalid file_ref resolution, storage I/O failure, and failure after streaming has begun?
options: All conditions that prevent delivery use the storage-unavailable error
Only missing or unreadable storage uses that error; policy refusals such as oversize or unlisted media use another outcome
Each failure class has a distinct outcome
set_aside.default_guess: Treat missing or unreadable bytes as storage-unavailable, and treat oversize or unlisted content as policy refusals.

witness.initial: An authorized viewer requests a visible ProgressPhoto whose stored bytes exist but exceed binary_max_read_bytes.
events: The viewer makes the authenticated binary-read request.
The portal recognizes that the photo exceeds the configured read bound.
outcomes: The portal returns the explicit storage-unavailable error because the content cannot be delivered.
The portal returns the concealed refusal used for an oversize document because oversize is a policy refusal rather than storage unavailability.
witness.observer: The viewer and any API client implementing retry or user messaging

set_aside.subject: R0-12 observable photo storage error
set_aside.question: What observable HTTP outcome identifies this error, including status, JSON error identifier and body, and whether it is the same for every qualifying photo failure?
options: A defined JSON error with a defined HTTP status
A defined HTTP status with no stable response body
Any implementation-specific response that is distinguishable from the concealed not-found outcome
set_aside.default_guess: Return a stable JSON error identifier with HTTP 503 before sending binary response headers.

witness.initial: An authorized viewer requests a visible ProgressPhoto whose file_ref resolves to no stored bytes.
events: The storage lookup reports that the bytes are unavailable.
outcomes: One implementation returns a typed JSON storage-unavailable error with HTTP 503.
Another returns an empty HTTP 500 response, regarding its distinct status as sufficiently explicit.
witness.observer: The viewer frontend, which must decide whether to show an unavailable-photo state or a generic server failure

set_aside.subject: R0-12 failure during photo streaming
set_aside.text: “An authorized document or photo is answered as its exact stored bytes” and “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: Must the portal verify or buffer the complete photo before committing the binary response so every delivery failure can become the explicit error, or may a read fail after response headers or partial bytes have been sent, in which case no explicit error response is possible?
options: Preflight or buffer the complete photo and return the explicit error before any bytes on failure
Stream directly and terminate the response if storage fails after streaming begins
Guarantee the explicit error only for failures detected before response commitment and specify the observable partial-stream outcome separately
set_aside.default_guess: Guarantee the explicit error only before response commitment and treat a later read failure as an aborted response.

witness.initial: A visible authorized photo is large enough to be streamed, and storage becomes unreadable after the first chunk.
events: The portal authorizes it and begins reading the file.
Storage returns an error after some bytes have been read.
outcomes: An implementation that buffered or preflighted the object sends only the explicit storage-unavailable error.
An implementation that streamed immediately has already sent a successful binary response and can only truncate or abort it.
witness.observer: The viewer and its HTTP client, which see either a structured failure or a corrupt/truncated download

set_aside.subject: R0-12 missing expense document versus explicit unavailable data
set_aside.text: R0-12 says “a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing,” while Client view says “Unavailable data is shown explicitly”
set_aside.question: When an authorized viewer requests a client-visible ExpenseDocument whose record exists but stored content is missing, must the client receive an explicit unavailable-data outcome or the same concealed outcome as an unknown, cross-project, or hidden object?
options: Use the concealed outcome required by R0-12
Expose an explicit unavailable-document outcome required by Client view
Keep the download concealed but expose availability explicitly in the authorized JSON document metadata
set_aside.default_guess: Keep the binary endpoint concealed as R0-12 requires and expose document availability in authorized client-view metadata.

witness.initial: A client-visible ExpenseDocument record belongs to a project granted to the viewer, but its stored binary is missing.
events: The viewer opens the project and sees the expense and document.
The viewer requests the document binary.
outcomes: R0-12 gives the same response as for an unknown or hidden document, so the viewer cannot identify missing data.
The Client view promise gives an explicit unavailable state, so the viewer can identify that the known document currently lacks deliverable content.
witness.observer: The viewer and frontend rendering the document’s availability
